feature: Search (F6) + Watchlist/Follow (F5) — one search box that resolves contract addresses, tickers and free text into a single ranked result set, and a star that turns "I'm waiting on this" into a push the moment a watched story mints.
summary: Search is Insidor's anti-duplicate surface: one box branches on contract address, $TICKER, or free text, and every branch answers the same question — does a coin already exist for this, and if so which one is real. Watchlist is not a list; it is a subscription to the 0→1 coin transition on a story, and the notification that fires when it happens is the retention hook the whole feature exists to deliver. Both surfaces obey the ONE RULE — the primary button is a pure function of the CONFIRMED coin count — and both render UNSURE matches visibly with the Buy affordance suppressed, per D1.
mechanism:
== 1. MODE DETECTION (features/search/model/parse.ts — pure, tested, no I/O) ==

parseQuery(raw) runs in this order and returns a discriminated union:

  CA      /^[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{32,44}$/ AND bs58.decode(q).length === 32
          (base58 alphabet excludes 0 O I l; the length test is what stops a 40-char
          English phrase with no spaces from claiming CA mode)
  TICKER  /^\$[A-Za-z0-9]{2,13}$/          → forced ticker mode ($ is an explicit intent)
          /^[A-Za-z0-9]{2,13}$/            → AMBIGUOUS: run ticker AND text, section both.
          13 = pump.fun symbol ceiling (DESIGN.md §6 F3.1). 2 = floor; 1 char is noise.
  HANDLE  /^@[A-Za-z0-9_]{1,15}$/          → poster mode (posts by handle)
  TEXT    everything else

Ambiguity is resolved by SHOWING both, never by guessing. "ferry" is both a plausible
ticker and a plausible keyword; the founder's rule ("keywords → both post and chart")
means the ambiguous case is the normal case, not an edge case.

== 2. RETRIEVAL — a three-retriever blend, fused by RRF ==

Why a blend and not one: the corpus is short, noisy social text. FTS alone dies on
typos, handles, emoji-heavy posts and cashtags. Trigram alone has no notion of
relevance across a document. Embeddings alone lose exact-token precision, which is
exactly what a ticker query needs. Each retriever covers the others' failure mode.

  R_fts    to_tsvector, GIN. Weighted:
             narratives:      A=title(simple)+subject_entity, B=title(english), C=blurb(english)
             narrative_posts: A=handle(simple), B=text(english)
           score = ts_rank_cd(search_doc, websearch_to_tsquery('english', q), 32)
           (normalisation 32 = divide by 1+log(doc length); short posts stop winning
           by being short)
  R_trgm   pg_trgm GIN over narratives.title, narrative_tickers.ticker,
           coin_index.symbol, coin_index.name, narrative_posts.handle
           score = similarity(col, q), threshold 0.30 (0.18 for ticker columns —
           ticker drift is 1–2 chars: FERRY/FERRIE/FERY)
  R_vec    pgvector HNSW (m=16, ef_construction=64, ef_search=64) over
           narratives.search_vec (story centroid) and post_embeddings.embedding
           score = 1 − (vec <=> embed(q))

Each retriever returns its own top 100. Fuse with weighted Reciprocal Rank Fusion —
chosen because the three scores are on incomparable scales and normalising them
requires a calibration set we do not have:

  RRF(d) = Σ_r  w_r / (60 + rank_r(d))       w_fts = 1.00, w_vec = 0.80, w_trgm = 0.60
  rel    = RRF(d) / max(RRF)                 → 0..1 within the result set

== 3. THE RANKING FORMULA (features/search/model/rank.ts — pure, tested) ==

  rec  = 1 / (1 + (age_min / 90)^1.1)
         age_min from narratives.promoted_at for stories, mint_time for coins,
         posted_at for posts. Half-life ≈ 90 min: a 90-min-old story ranks 0.5,
         a day-old story 0.06. This is a terminal, not an archive.
  vir  = ln(1 + heat) / ln(1 + 100)
         heat = the presented 0..100 heat from the §4.2 ranking primitive
         (base = rate_LCB_norm × burst^0.5 ; heat = (base·O·D)^0.85 / ((age+12)/12)^1.35 × C).
         For coins, vir uses CoinHeat_live / p95_CoinHeat_1h.
  score = (0.55·rel + 0.25·vir + 0.20·rec) × boost × typePrior

  boost   ×1.35  exact ticker equality (q strips $, uppercased, == narrative_tickers.ticker
                 or coin_index.symbol)
          ×1.15  q is a case-insensitive substring of narratives.title
          ×1.05  story has ≥1 CONFIRMED coin (an actionable result is a better result)
          ×0.60  narratives.needs_review = true (coherence < 0.55 — garbage-bag story)
          ×0.00  coinability_tier = 'never'  → hard-filtered BEFORE ranking, not down-weighted
  typePrior  story 1.00 · coin 0.95 · post 0.80

Relevance dominates at 0.55 because a search box that reorders your query by
popularity is a trending board wearing a search box.

== 4. DEDUPE / ROLL-UP — how three object types become one result set ==

Sectioned, not interleaved: three shapes with three column grammars, and a terminal
user scans columns. But one interleaving rule makes the set feel like one answer:

  a) A POST whose narrative_id already appears in the Stories section is NOT listed
     separately. It folds into that story row as "+3 more posts match" (expands inline).
  b) A COIN whose narrative_id already appears in Stories renders in BOTH places —
     inline in the story row's coin strip, and in the Coins section with its chart
     columns. This is the founder's rule made literal: keyword → post AND chart.
  c) The single highest-scoring object of any kind is lifted out into a BEST MATCH
     strip above all sections, resolved to exactly one action. Ties broken by
     typePrior, then earlier promoted_at.

== 5. SNIPPETS

  ts_headline('english', text, websearch_to_tsquery(q),
              'MaxFragments=1, MaxWords=18, MinWords=8, StartSel=<mark>, StopSel=</mark>')
  <mark> styled background:rgba(61,224,255,.18); color:var(--ink); border-radius:2px.
  Never truncate mid-<mark>.

== 6. CA RESOLUTION LADDER (each rung is a cache write-through to the next request)

  1. narrative_tickers.mint = $1           → coin known, story known           ~4 ms
  2. coin_index.mint = $1                  → coin known, story unknown         ~4 ms
  3. GET /api/token-lookup?mint=           → DexScreener live, cold resolve  ~250 ms
     mint_time = min(pairCreatedAt) across ALL pairs (§5.3), NEVER best-pair.
     Missing pairCreatedAt → mint_time = null → UNKNOWN → Buy suppressed. Never 0.
  4. RPC getAccountInfo owner check        → is this even a token?           ~120 ms
     owner ≠ Tokenkeg…/TokenzQd… → render "That's a wallet, not a token."
  5. Nothing anywhere → "Valid Solana address. No pair, no story, no post."
     This is a result, not an error, and it is rendered as one.

  In parallel with 1–3, always: SELECT posts WHERE text ILIKE '%'||$1||'%' — a mint
  literally typed into a tracked post is S_mint_in_post = 1.00, the strongest evidence
  channel the matcher has, and it is what the founder means by "search CA, post appears".

== 7. TICKER FAMILY — the anti-duplicate mechanism

  For $FERRY, list every live Solana mint with that exact symbol, SORTED BY MINT TIME
  ASCENDING. Not by volume, not by mcap. Rationale from §5.2: conditional on an exact
  symbol, competing mints are separated by MONTHS (TRUMP: 7 mints / 563 days), so the
  earliest is almost always the real one and every later one is a copycat. Every
  incumbent sorts this list by volume, which ranks the copycat that got pumped.

  collision_idf(sym) = log(1 + N_total / (1 + N_symbol)) / log(1 + N_total)
  rendered as a plain-English line, not a number: "PUMP is a common ticker — 4 live
  coins share it" vs "FERRY is rare — 1 live coin."

== 8. NOTIFICATION TRIGGER

  Fires on the transition confirmed_coin_count(narrative) : 0 → ≥1, and ONLY on
  match_status = 'confirmed'. UNSURE never notifies — pushing "your story minted" on a
  0.6-confidence match is the exact failure the D1 abstain band exists to prevent, and
  it is unrecoverable trust damage. An UNSURE row that later promotes to CONFIRMED does
  notify (in-app only, no push — the earliness is already spent).

  AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE ON narrative_tickers
    WHEN (NEW.match_status = 'confirmed' AND COALESCE(OLD.match_status,'') <> 'confirmed')
    → enqueue_mint_notifications(NEW.narrative_id, NEW.mint)
      → INSERT INTO notification (…) SELECT … FROM follow
        WHERE narrative_id = NEW.narrative_id AND notify_mint <> 'muted'
          AND (muted_until IS NULL OR muted_until < now())
        ON CONFLICT (dedupe_key) DO NOTHING
      → realtime.send(payload, 'mint', 'user:'||user_id, private := true)

  dedupe_key = user_id || ':' || narrative_id || ':' || date_trunc('hour', now())/6
  Coalesce window: all coins confirmed within 90 s of the first collapse into ONE
  notification (copycat swarms mint 3–8 coins in under a minute). If 2+ coins land in
  the window the message becomes "got 3 coins in 90 seconds" and the primary button is
  "See the 3 coins" — the ONE RULE, enforced inside the notification.
  Follow-up: at most one, only if a later coin's peak mcap > 4× the first AND the first
  peaked under $25k, labelled "a bigger coin appeared".

  Latency budget, mint → glass: PumpPortal ws → matcher 3–8 s → confirm → trigger
  <1 s → Broadcast ~60 ms. p50 < 20 s, p90 < 60 s. Web Push adds 2–10 s. A 5-minute
  notification on a product that sells 20-minute head starts is worth nothing; this
  budget is a product requirement, not an SLO.

== 9. QUERY SHAPES

  -- fused search, one round trip
  CREATE FUNCTION search_all(q text, q_vec vector, k int DEFAULT 40)
  RETURNS TABLE(kind text, id uuid, rrf real) AS $$
    WITH fts AS (
      SELECT 'story'::text kind, id,
             row_number() OVER (ORDER BY ts_rank_cd(search_doc,
               websearch_to_tsquery('english', q), 32) DESC) rnk
      FROM narratives
      WHERE search_doc @@ websearch_to_tsquery('english', q)
        AND promoted_at IS NOT NULL
        AND status IN ('open','dormant')
        AND coinability_tier <> 'never'
      LIMIT 100),
    trg AS (
      SELECT 'story', id, row_number() OVER (ORDER BY similarity(title, q) DESC)
      FROM narratives WHERE title % q AND coinability_tier <> 'never' LIMIT 100),
    vec AS (
      SELECT 'story', id, row_number() OVER (ORDER BY search_vec <=> q_vec)
      FROM narratives WHERE search_vec IS NOT NULL
      ORDER BY search_vec <=> q_vec LIMIT 100)
    SELECT kind, id,
           SUM(w / (60 + rnk))::real
    FROM (SELECT *, 1.00 w FROM fts UNION ALL
          SELECT *, 0.60 w FROM trg UNION ALL
          SELECT *, 0.80 w FROM vec) u
    GROUP BY kind, id ORDER BY 3 DESC LIMIT k;
  $$ LANGUAGE sql STABLE;
  -- (the same CTE shape repeats for kind='post' over narrative_posts and
  --  kind='coin' over narrative_tickers ⋈ coin_index; three parallel calls, not one
  --  giant union, so a slow vector leg cannot stall the text legs)

  -- "No coin yet" chip
  SELECT n.*, COUNT(t.*) FILTER (WHERE t.match_status='unsure') AS unsure_n
  FROM narratives n LEFT JOIN narrative_tickers t ON t.narrative_id = n.id
  WHERE n.promoted_at IS NOT NULL AND n.status IN ('open','dormant')
    AND n.coinability_tier <> 'never'
    AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM narrative_tickers c
                    WHERE c.narrative_id = n.id AND c.match_status='confirmed')
  GROUP BY n.id ORDER BY n.heat DESC LIMIT 50;

  -- Finished chip, default filter = ALL (D2)
  SELECT * FROM story_outcome
  WHERE resolved_at > now() - interval '7 days'
  ORDER BY resolved_at DESC LIMIT 100;    -- outcome IN ('early','late','no_coin','flat','unresolved')

  -- Following
  SELECT f.*, n.*, c.* FROM follow f
  LEFT JOIN narratives n ON n.id = f.narrative_id
  LEFT JOIN coin_index c ON c.mint = f.coin_mint
  WHERE f.user_id = $1 OR f.device_id = $2
  ORDER BY f.created_at DESC;

== 10. LATENCY CONTRACT
  Palette local index (last board tick, ~200 stories + ~400 coins held in the store):
  answers every keystroke in <16 ms, zero network.
  Server: FTS+trgm path p95 < 120 ms. Vector leg adds ~30 ms and is rendered as it
  arrives (the text legs never wait on it). Debounce 180 ms in the palette, 250 ms on
  the full surface. Request-sequence guard (the existing extSearchReq pattern) so a
  slow leg never overwrites a newer query's results.

⌘K/Ctrl-K opens from anywhere; pressing it AGAIN closes. '/' opens when no input is focused. ↑/↓ move through a FLAT index across all sections (section headers are skipped, never selectable). ⌘↑/⌘↓ jump to the previous/next section head. Enter opens the selection. ⌘Enter abandons the preview and opens /search?q= with the full surface. Tab accepts the top ticker/entity completion INTO the input (completion, not navigation — Tab must never navigate). S stars the highlighted row in place, with a lime flash and no close. Backspace on an empty input clears the mode chip. Esc closes and restores focus to whatever had it. Focus is trapped inside .pal while open; body overflow hidden.

elements.element: Relationship to the full Search surface
elements.interaction: The palette is a PROJECTION of /search, never a parallel implementation: same parse, same search_all(), same ranking, same row components at smaller sizes. Two consequences. (1) When the user is ALREADY on /search, ⌘K does not open the overlay — it focuses and selects the page input, which is exactly the flow doc's 'Cmd K now just focuses the search field'. (2) The palette can do strictly LESS than the surface: it navigates and it stars. It cannot buy, cannot create, cannot filter by chip. Anything that spends money or mints a token requires the full surface and a deliberate click.

screens.layout: Not a screen — a 3-state control with four host treatments. (a) Table rows: .star inline in .nar-title-line / .tksym — background none, var(--dim), 13px, hover var(--ion) + scale(1.15), .on var(--ion). Glyph ☆/★. (b) Story page header: .tbtn-watch — mono 11.5px, var(--bg2) ground, 1px rgba(255,255,255,.07), radius 8, padding 5px 11px; labels '☆ Watch' / '★ Watching'. (c) Coin page trade panel: same .tbtn-watch in .tb-head. (d) Palette: no visible control, the S key.

elements.shows: A STORY or a COIN. Never a post.
elements.interaction: A post is evidence, not a subject: posts get pruned, merged and re-parented (§3.4), so a follow on one would silently die or silently move. The story is the durable object and it is what the notification is about. On a post detail modal the ★ therefore stars the post's STORY, and the label says so: '★ Watching this story'.

elements.shows: When a watched story mints, the follow row REMAINS a story follow. The Following list shows the story row with a coin strip nested inside it; the coin does not become its own row.
elements.interaction: The notification and the story row both offer an explicit secondary 'Watch $CUPS too', which writes a SECOND follow row with coin_mint set. Migrating the follow would destroy exactly what the user asked for — they asked about a story, and a story can mint again.

Buying a coin auto-follows THE COIN. Creating a coin auto-follows the coin AND its story. Commenting on a story auto-follows the story. These are not silent conversions — each is a deliberate financial or social act by the user, and each is announced by a 2-second toast 'Following $CUPS' with an inline Undo. Everything you touch appears in You; nothing appears that you did not touch.

elements.shows: The ★ works with no wallet and no account.
elements.source: follow.device_id ⚠new column, a uuid in localStorage['insidor_device']
elements.interaction: On first Privy login, all device_id follows are claimed by the user_id in one UPDATE. Conflicts (same target already followed by the account) resolve by keeping the EARLIER created_at, because the earlier follow is the one with the honest lead time. Flow doc: 'You do not need a wallet to do that.'

elements.shows: A 3-state control adjacent to the ★ on Following rows only, not in tables: All (every coin, every reopen) · Mint only (DEFAULT) · Muted. Rendered as a 14px bell glyph — filled cyan / outline / struck-through dim.
elements.interaction: Click cycles; long-press or right-click on the ★ anywhere in the app opens the same 3-way menu without navigating.

elements.shows: Fills instantly, lime flash 240ms.
elements.interaction: Replaces the prototype's refreshWatchStars() which re-rendered SIX views for one boolean — and which could fire a network search as a side effect. One store write, memoised rows.

states: off / on / pending (optimistic, reverts with a 'couldn't save' toast on failure)
anonymous (device) — fully functional; a dim mono 9px 'saved to this device' appears once, on the first ever follow, and never again
already followed via auto-follow — the ★ is on and its tooltip explains why: 'Following since you bought'
story is tier 'never' — unreachable; those stories are never rendered
offline — queued in localStorage, flushed on reconnect

screens.name: Following — /you (Watchlist)
screens.job: Turn 'I'm waiting on this' into a scannable board, and make an empty one teach instead of sit blank.
screens.layout: Sections stacked, each a .wl-section with .wl-section-hd (Clash 15px title, mono 11px count, right-aligned section action). A section renders only when non-empty (flow doc rule), EXCEPT when all are empty, in which case the teaching empty state replaces the whole screen. Section order is fixed by urgency, not by recency: (1) Just minted · (2) Waiting — no coin yet · (3) With coins · (4) Coins you watch · (5) Gone quiet (collapsed).

elements.shows: Stories you follow that got a CONFIRMED coin in the last 24h and that you have not opened. Row = .sr-narr with .ntk.narr-pinned treatment (inset 3px lime left edge + 1px rgba(155,240,60,.18) ring) and a lime NEW pin. The row's second line is the payload: 'Wrong Name is now $CUPS · minted 2m after we saw it · $18.4K'.
elements.source: notification WHERE kind='mint' AND read_at IS NULL ⚠new table
elements.interaction: Primary button resolves by CONFIRMED count (Buy $CUPS / See the 3 coins). Opening the row clears the pin. Section disappears when empty — it is not a permanent header.

elements.shows: Same row spec as the No-coin-yet chip, minus the rank column. Adds a mono 10px 'watched 2h ago' on the right.
elements.interaction: Inline Create per row (D3 tier respected). This is the section the notification is a promise about.

elements.shows: Story rows whose primary resolves to Buy or See-the-N. Each carries a nested coin strip: up to 3 chips, mono 11px, '$CUPS $18.4K' with the .match-stamp inline.
elements.interaction: Coin chip → coin page. A dim '+ Watch $CUPS too' at the end of the strip writes the separate coin follow — the explicit, never-silent conversion.

elements.shows: The .tk 11-column table: Token · Price · 5m · 1h · 24h · Last 24h spark · Volume · Liquidity · Mkt cap · Age · action. Plus a Story column replacing the sparkline below 1180px.
elements.source: follow WHERE coin_mint IS NOT NULL ⋈ coin_index ⚠new
elements.interaction: SORTABLE headers. This is a deliberate deviation from the prototype (§4.5/§12.10 note that watchlist headers omit .sortable) — a 40-coin watchlist without sort is unusable, and the reason the prototype omitted it was a session-Set implementation, not a design decision.

elements.shows: Collapsed header only: 'Gone quiet (7) — dormant over 24h, still no coin'. Expands to dim rows at .72 opacity.
elements.source: follow ⋈ narratives WHERE status='dormant' AND updated_at < now()−24h AND confirmed_coin_count=0
elements.interaction: Per-row 'Stop watching', plus a header action 'Clear all 7'. This section exists because watchlist rot — 60 dead rows above the 3 live ones — is the actual reason watchlists get abandoned. Rows here still notify; going quiet is not the same as being over.

elements.shows: .chips in the tbar: Recently added (default) · Heat · Lead time · Coin status.
elements.interaction: Sorts within each section; never merges sections.

elements.shows: Centered block, max-width 480px, no dashed box. Clash 20px 'Nothing watched yet.' Then 13.5px muted: 'Tap ★ on any story and we'll tell you the moment somebody mints it. No wallet needed.' Then a full-width sub-header 'Three worth watching right now' and THREE REAL LIVE ROWS from the No-coin-yet list (top 3 by heat), each with an inline ★ that fills in place without navigating and a lead chip so the value is legible before the user commits. Then a dim mono 11px stat line, rendered only when the number is real: 'Last week, 61% of watched stories got a coin within 3 hours. 34% never did.'
elements.source: the No-coin-yet query, limit 3, ORDER BY heat DESC; the stat from story_outcome ⚠new
elements.interaction: Starring one of the three converts the empty state IN PLACE into a one-row Section 2 — the user sees the mechanism work in one gesture with no navigation. The honest 34% is included because a retention hook that oversells its hit rate gets uninstalled after the first miss.

elements.shows: Right of the Following header: a 14px bell glyph with a mono 10px count of enabled channels ('in-app' / 'in-app + push').
elements.interaction: Opens the settings sheet (see the notification screen).

states: empty — the teaching state above, which is the highest-leverage state on this screen
anonymous (device follows) — everything works; a persistent dim banner 'Saved to this device. Connect a wallet to keep these on your phone too.' with a Connect link
one section only — no visual gap where the others would be

story merged into another — the follow silently repoints to the survivor (§3.4 says repoint watchlist entries) and the row shows a dim 'merged into <title>' caption for 24h. This is the ONE case where the target changes, and it is disclosed
story closed with no coin ever — moves to Gone quiet, then after 7 days to a 'Ended without a coin' fold with a Clear action. Never silently deleted
unverified match on a watched story — the row shows the amber sub-line and does NOT move to Section 3; an unverified match is not a coin
coin watched but no market data — '—' across, 'no market yet'
stale pipeline — banner
loading — 3 skeleton rows, sections not yet known (do not render section headers before their counts, or empty headers flash)

screens.name: The mint notification — end to end
screens.job: Deliver 'the story you followed just got a coin' fast enough that the head start survives the delivery.
screens.layout: Four surfaces, one event. (A) In-app toast: fixed bottom-right, 24px inset, width 380px, z-index 400, .note-card skin (linear-gradient(180deg,var(--bg2),var(--bg1)), 1px var(--line), radius 14, padding 13) with a 2px lime left edge and slidein .45s. (B) While-you-were-away band: full-width, position 1 on Trending ABOVE the pinned proof card, 88px, .ttable skin with a lime left edge. (C) Web Push: OS notification with icon = the token logo, badge = the Insidor dot. (D) Settings sheet: .sheet max-width 472px.

elements.shows: Clash 15px: 'Wrong Name is now $CUPS'. The STORY name first, the ticker second — the user followed a story and must recognise it before they parse a ticker.
mono 11px: 'Minted 2m ago · $18.4K · you're 31m early'. When lead is negative: 'Minted 2m ago · $18.4K · crypto traders got here 6m before us.' — same slot, same size, grey instead of lime.
elements.interaction: D2 carried into the push: the number that carries the product is shown even when it is bad. A notification that only fires on wins is an ad.

elements.shows: A two-button row: primary .deploy-go (resolves by CONFIRMED count — 'Buy $CUPS' / 'See the 3 coins'), secondary bordered 'See story'. Below both, a dim 11px link 'Watch $CUPS too'.
elements.interaction: Buy opens the Jupiter modal in place, no navigation — the toast is the trade entry point and every navigation between the alert and the buy costs seconds the product just spent 20 minutes earning. 'Watch $CUPS too' is the explicit, never-silent story→coin conversion.

Auto-dismisses at 12s, PAUSED on hover. Never auto-dismisses while the Jupiter modal it opened is on screen. Max 3 stacked; a fourth collapses the stack into '3 stories you follow got coins' → opens Following. Delivered on the existing ref-counted Supabase socket via a private 'user:{id}' topic folded into the board tick envelope — zero new transport, zero new failure modes.

elements.shows: '1 story you follow got a coin.' Clash 16px, then the coin row inline (36px icon, $CUPS, mcap, age) and the resolved primary button. Multi: '3 stories you follow got coins' with the top one expanded and '+2 more'.
elements.source: notification WHERE read_at IS NULL AND created_at > last_session_end
elements.interaction: Renders on the next app open when the tab was closed or hidden at fire time. Persists until dismissed or 24h. Dismiss marks read. This is what replaces the alerts inbox — the flow doc CUT the inbox on the grounds that 'While you were away' answers 'what did I miss' better, and this band is that answer.

elements.shows: An inline button INSIDE the first while-you-were-away band: 'Get this on your phone next time' + a dim 11px 'These move in minutes. We only send this one thing.'
elements.interaction: NEVER prompted on first load, never on signup, never in a modal. The prompt appears exactly once, at the moment the user has just experienced the value and simultaneously discovered they missed it live. That is the highest-converting placement available and it costs nothing to wait for it. Declining hides the ask for 30 days.

elements.shows: Title 'Wrong Name is now $CUPS'. Body 'The story you followed just got its first coin. Minted 2m ago · $18.4K · you're 31m early.' Icon = token logo (Helius getAsset), badge = the cyan Insidor dot. Actions: 'Buy' and 'See story'. Tag = narrative_id (so a follow-up REPLACES rather than stacks).
elements.interaction: Deep-links to /coin/[mint]?src=push. The src param feeds search_log-style attribution so the retention claim is measurable rather than assumed.

elements.shows: DAILY DIGEST ONLY, opt-in, off by default: 'Yesterday: 3 stories you follow got coins.' with a 3-row table and each row's lead time.
elements.interaction: Per-mint email is explicitly REJECTED: email arrives long after the trade is over, and one useless real-time email teaches the user to filter the sender forever. Email's job here is the weekly reminder that the product exists, not the alert.

elements.source: AFTER trigger on narrative_tickers, WHEN match_status transitions to 'confirmed'
elements.interaction: ONLY CONFIRMED fires. UNSURE never fires anything — a push claiming 'your story minted' on a 0.6-confidence match is the single most damaging output this system can produce, and the D1 abstain band exists precisely to make it impossible. An UNSURE that later promotes to CONFIRMED fires IN-APP ONLY, with the honest lead ('we confirmed this 40m after it minted'), and never a push.

One per (user, narrative) per 6h. All coins confirmed within 90s collapse into one message; 2+ makes the copy 'Wrong Name got 3 coins in 90 seconds' and the button 'See the 3 coins' — the ONE RULE enforced inside the notification, because the copycat swarm is exactly when a user is most likely to buy the wrong one. At most one follow-up, only when a later coin's peak > 4× the first and the first peaked under $25k, labelled 'a bigger coin appeared'.

elements.shows: Rows: 'In-app alerts — always on' (disabled toggle with a dim 'this is the product'), 'Push' (toggle + browser permission state), 'Quiet hours' (two time pickers + tz), 'Only if the coin passes safety checks' (toggle, default ON — suppresses pushes for mint-authority-active / top-10>60% coins), 'Minimum market cap' (None / $10k / $50k), 'Daily email digest' (off by default).
elements.interaction: Reachable from the Following header bell, from any toast's ⋯, and from the push itself. Every alert product dies from being un-tunable; three knobs is the whole budget.

states: fired, tab focused → toast
fired, tab hidden or closed → queued → while-you-were-away band on next open (+ push if enabled)
fired, quiet hours → held, delivered as the first band on next open, with a dim 'held during quiet hours'
push permission denied → the ask hides for 30 days; in-app never degrades
push subscription expired (410 from the push service) → row deleted, fail_count incremented, a one-time in-app 'push stopped working — re-enable?'
coin fails safety and the safety toggle is on → no push, but the in-app band still shows it with a red Risky pill (suppressing it entirely would be hiding information the user asked for)
UNSURE match — no notification of any kind; the Following row shows the amber sub-line so the user is not blind
multi-coin swarm → one coalesced message, See-the-N primary
story merged before the mint → notification fires on the SURVIVOR narrative and names it, with a dim 'this story merged with <title>'
offline at fire time → Broadcast is missed; the band is the backstop, hydrated from the notification table on next load. The table is the source of truth; the socket is only the fast path
wallet not connected → notification fires normally (follows do not need a wallet); the Buy button opens connect first

buildOrder: 1. MIGRATION A — the correctness floor. Add narrative_tickers.mint, .source, .relation, .match_status, .match_score, .match_channels, .mint_time; add narratives.promoted_at (set-once, never-clobber, same pattern as cluster-persist.js:46-58), .heat, .coinability_tier, .needs_review. Backfill mint from the DexScreener path token-lookup.js already resolves and currently discards. Ship NOTHING else until this lands — every screen in this spec computes its primary button from confirmed_coin_count, and today that number does not exist.

2. Replace lib/types.ts storyAction()'s `ticker && mcap != null` test with `match_status === 'confirmed'`, and add the .match-stamp component. This alone removes the live 'Buy $KANG' bug from every existing surface. Two files, immediate user-visible correctness win.

3. MIGRATION B — search plumbing. Generated search_doc tsvector on narratives and narrative_posts + GIN; pg_trgm GIN on narratives.title, narrative_tickers.ticker, narrative_posts.handle; search_log table. No UI yet.

4. Ship /search free-text, FTS + trigram only, no embeddings, no chips. Rank = (0.55·rel + 0.25·vir + 0.20·rec) × boost, RRF over two retrievers. Sections: Stories, Coins, Posts. Includes the zero-result Create block — the highest-value 40 lines in the feature. URL-driven (?q=), which also gives the app its first linkable route.

5. CA mode: the four-rung resolution ladder over the new .mint column with the existing /api/token-lookup?mint= as rung 3, plus the mint-in-post band. Ships with the fail-closed rule replacing token-lookup.js:70 `return 0`.

6. $TICKER mode + the ticker family table sorted by mint time ascending, with the .coll availability line lifted verbatim from the create sheet. This is the anti-duplicate job delivered; it is shippable before the indexer using live DexScreener symbol search, just slower and less complete.
7. ⌘K palette over the same server route, local-index-first. Zero new backend. Includes the on-/search ⌘K-focuses-the-field reconciliation with the flow doc.

8. MIGRATION C — app_user, follow (with device_id, notify_mint, muted_until, last_notified_at), notification, notification_prefs. Wire ★ to one store with an optimistic toggle, replacing the two in-memory Sets and the six-view refreshWatchStars() cascade.

9. Following screen: sections 2, 3, 4 and the teaching empty state with three live starrable rows. Ships before any notification exists — the list is useful on its own and it is the surface the notification will point at.

10. THE NOTIFICATION, in-app only: the AFTER trigger on confirmed matches, the dedupe key, the 90-second coalescing window, the user:{id} Broadcast topic folded into the existing socket, the toast, and the while-you-were-away band. This is the retention hook and it MUST NOT wait behind push — in-app plus the band already delivers the J2 journey end to end.

11. Web Push: push_subscription, VAPID, service worker, the earned-moment permission prompt inside the first band, quiet hours, the safety-gate toggle. Measure push→buy conversion via ?src=push before spending anything more on it.

12. Chips, in value order: No coin yet (with D3 tier gating — do NOT ship a browsable candidate list before coinability_tier exists and is populated) → Just made with the From-a-story-only toggle → Trending now with the four coin-lane bands.

13. The two prospective clocks: persist t_mint from the PumpPortal websocket and t_ct from the ~300 polled CT accounts. Then the story_outcome materialized view. Then the Finished chip with All-default and the honest summary header. Finished cannot ship before this, and shipping a record from lead_time_min alone would be fabricating the product's central claim.

14. pgvector recall: narratives.search_vec centroid + HNSW, added as a third RRF leg. A/B the blend weights against search_log click-through — the 0.55/0.25/0.20 numbers are a starting guess and should not survive contact with real data unchanged.

15. Coin index integration (F3.2): coin_index table, the mint stream, and CA/ticker search over mints that never touched a story. Also unlocks the rail's Matches mode and the true 'N coins share this ticker' count.
openQuestions: The command palette is CUT in docs/product/insidor-flow.html ('A search box wearing a keyboard shortcut. Cmd K now just focuses the search field') and REQUIRED by this brief. I have specced the reconciliation — the palette is a strict projection of /search with no private query path and no capability beyond navigate+star, and on /search itself ⌘K focuses the field rather than opening an overlay. Confirm that reconciliation or kill the overlay.

Do anonymous device_id follows survive to a Privy account, and what wins on conflict? I specced: claim on first login, keep the EARLIER created_at because that follow has the honest lead time. Also: a follow made on a laptop is invisible on a phone until login — is that acceptable for v1, or does the ★ gate on connect after the first three follows?

Push on iOS requires the PWA to be installed to the home screen. Is web push therefore an Android/desktop-only feature at launch, with iOS users on in-app + band only? If iOS matters, this becomes a native-app question and it is the largest scope item in the feature.

Does an UNSURE match that later promotes to CONFIRMED notify at all? I specced yes, in-app only, no push, with the lead rendered honestly ('confirmed 40m after it minted'). The counter-argument is that a stale alert is worse than none.

Is $50k peak mcap the right EARLY/FLAT boundary in story_outcome? It sets the headline hit rate on the Finished chip and therefore the number the whole track record is judged on. Pick it from the existing 1,041-narrative backfill, not from taste.

Does Finished include stories where a coin exists but our matcher never confirmed it? I specced YES, as an UNRESOLVED outcome, on the grounds that hiding the cases where our own matcher gave up is precisely the marketing D2 forbids. Confirm — it will make the record look worse and that is the point.

Saved searches / 'Watch this search — we'll tell you if a story shows up' in the zero-result state. It is the natural bridge between the two features and it turns the best empty state into a follow. It also needs a saved_search table and a second notification kind. In or out for v1?

Verify post_embeddings.embedding's dimension AND its model. Query-time embedding must use the same one, and if it is a worker-side model the search path gains a network hop — is that inside the p95 < 120ms budget, or does the vector leg have to render asynchronously (which is what I specced as the fallback)?

How far back does search reach? I specced open|dormant in the default set with closed reachable only via the Finished chip. A user searching a two-week-old story by name will get nothing and that will read as a bug.

Who populates narratives.coinability_tier, and how? D3 is a policy with three tiers judged on 'is there an identifiable person harmed by this becoming a coin'. Nothing in the current pipeline computes it. The No-coin-yet chip is the most exposed surface in the product — a browsable, one-tap-mintable list — and it cannot ship before this field is real and evaluated. This is the single largest unowned dependency in the spec.

Does the mint notification's Buy button open Jupiter in place inside the toast? window.Jupiter is a global singleton with one integratedTargetId (§7.3), so a toast-mounted trade panel may conflict with an already-open one. Verify the singleton can be retargeted, or the toast falls back to navigating.

The 0.55/0.25/0.20 relevance/virality/recency weights and the ×1.35/×1.15 boosts are a defensible starting guess, not a measurement. search_log exists in this spec specifically to replace them. Who owns that tuning pass, and at what query volume does it become meaningful?
priorArt: Reciprocal Rank Fusion (Cormack, Clarke & Buettcher, SIGIR 2009) — chosen over score normalisation because ts_rank_cd, trigram similarity and cosine distance are on incomparable scales and normalising them correctly needs a calibration set we do not have. k=60 is the paper's constant and it is robust; the per-retriever weights are ours.

PostgreSQL ts_rank_cd with normalisation flag 32 (divide by 1+log(length)) and ts_headline for fragment generation — standard, already available on Supabase, and it removes the need for any external search service at this corpus size (1,041 narratives, 1,718 posts today).

pg_trgm GIN for fuzzy ticker and handle matching. Ticker drift in this domain is 1–2 characters (FERRY/FERRIE/FERY), which is exactly the regime trigram similarity handles and exactly where FTS returns nothing.

Linear and Superhuman command palettes — the flat-index-across-sections keyboard model, ⌘Enter as the escape to full results, and the rule that the palette navigates but never mutates. The 13-row cap comes from the same lineage: a palette you scroll has become a worse search page.

DexScreener / Photon same-symbol collision lists — adopted as a pattern, INVERTED in ordering. They sort by volume, which surfaces whichever copycat got pumped; we sort by mint time ascending because §5.2 measured that competing same-symbol mints are separated by months, making the earliest almost always the real one.

GitHub's three-state watch control (All activity / Releases only / Ignore) as the model for All / Mint only / Muted. 'Releases only' is structurally the same product insight as 'Mint only': the one state change you actually care about, not the firehose.

Robinhood and Coinbase price alerts for the notify-on-event retention loop. The Insidor difference is that the event is a MINT, not a price — it happens once, it is irreversible, and being 40 minutes late to it is worthless, which is why the p50 < 20s budget is a product requirement rather than an SLO.

Photon's freeze-on-hover and never-reflow-below-the-fold list behaviours (already adopted in §4.3) — carried into the search result set so a live-updating result list does not move under the cursor mid-click.

The prototype's own .pal / .pal-search palette shell, .sr-narr search rows, .tk token table, .coll availability line, .tp-origin strip, .tbtn-watch and .star — all reused verbatim from docs/research/design-component-inventory.md. Exactly two components are new: .match-stamp (the categorical confidence chip) and .sr-post (the post result row).

§5.9 of docs/research/03-system-design.md on categorical-not-numeric confidence — 'do not render 73% match next to an actionable control, users treat 73% as good enough and do their own thresholding, which defeats the abstain band entirely'. match_score is stored for calibration and never rendered anywhere in this spec.
